summary.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,217 crore (+19.8% YoY), PAT Rs 46.9 crore (~4x YoY), EBITDA margin 17.96%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was flat QoQ at Rs 1,217 crore and up 19.84% YoY, with EBITDA excluding other income at Rs 218.47 crore (up 47% YoY, 5% QoQ). EBITDA margin rose to 17.96% from 17.11% in Q4, while management said energy and shipping costs were not fully passed on. Net debt fell about Rs 100 crore QoQ to around Rs 1,900 crore, and management reiterated a Rs 500 crore leverage reduction target for FY27. Management guided to strong export growth, a wheels JV and rail trial ramp-up, and a multi-year non-ferrous (aluminium, titanium, Inconel) push.

financial_highlights.change: from 17.11% in previous quarter (+85 bps QoQ)
Up ~535 bps QoQ per analyst question; management said it is sustainable
Down ~Rs 100 crore from Rs 1,990 crore last quarter
Per analyst question; not stated by management

segments.name: Automotive (order wins)
segments.commentary: Secured Rs 278 crore of business with a four-year program life; ~82% passenger vehicle and ~18% two-wheeler, all domestic. Passenger vehicle split roughly 50:50 ICE vs EV per management.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Won Rs 15 crore of Metro orders from Indian Railways. Rail wheel JV (RKTR) trial production has started; first 300 sample wheels to be submitted in August.

segments.name: Mexico
segments.commentary: Production started; about Rs 6 crore of revenue booked this quarter, with significant revenue expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Aluminium / non-ferrous
segments.commentary: Bulk supplies of aluminium forgings have started. Management says meaningful contribution from aerospace/semiconductor/robotics is 12-18 months away, with Inconel/titanium 8-10 quarters away.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated ROCE targeted at 12-15%; FY28 target 20%.
Exports expected at about 35% of consolidated revenue for FY27 and growth of 'almost 20% plus' in exports; management called it possibly the highest export revenue ever.
Net debt reduction of at least Rs 500 crore in FY27 (implying ~Rs 1,500 crore by year-end), per management.
FY27 capex guidance around Rs 350 crore, plus Rs 20-30 crore further investment into the rail wheel JV.
Turnover target of Rs 8,000 crore now pegged to FY29 (one year later than earlier), implying 22-25% CAGR.
Working capital: internal target of 15-20 days improvement across debtor, inventory and creditor days, with management suggesting roughly 10 days per year.
Cold forging capacity utilisation expected above 70% by Q3 FY27; sustainable utilisation of 75-80% before next capex.
Rail wheel plant: bulk production targeted for Sept/Oct 2026 with full contractual supply to Railways thereafter.
capex_capacity: Majority of strategic capex is complete; focus shifted to utilisation and asset turn. Management cited asset turn of 2.5x on ~Rs 3,700 crore net block implying ~Rs 9,000 crore sales at 100% utilisation, though it said 75-80% is the practical ceiling.
Ring rolling capacity at 127% utilisation; management said no plans to add ring rolling capacity and expects peak utilisation for two to three years.
A new press line is being added; it will take four to five quarters to reach about 80% press utilisation.
Casting plant capitalised in Q4 FY26; integration substantially complete and capacity ramp-up expected over the next three quarters.
Aluminium forging capability in place; Inconel/titanium capex limited to about Rs 10-20 crore for heating arrangements.
Wheel JV: 80,000 confirmed Railway wheel order plus about 25,000 wheels from JV partners (~1,10,000 total), covering production until end FY28. Major new capex to be announced only by end FY28.
demand_pricing: Management described the order book as strong, with healthy domestic demand, and expects the next half (after monsoon, around September) to be exciting domestically.
Export growth driven by Europe and North America, with new orders from existing and new customers; customer names not disclosed.
Steel is passed through with a one-quarter lag; gas, energy and shipping costs are not fully passed on. No hedging available for steel.
Currency is passed through every quarter on all contracts, per management, so rupee depreciation (1-1.5% in quarter) gives no net benefit.

Domestic realisation rose QoQ on better mix, higher utilisation and product choice. Casting realisations declined QoQ due to one-off components run during capacity ramp-up; management expects recovery.
Management said it would not guide on profitability or a full-year margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin rise only 85 bps QoQ when gross margin rose ~535 bps? Is it only price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied it was only price, citing product mix. It said energy and shipping costs have not been passed on, which limited EBITDA margin gains; improvement should follow once costs stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Are there target ROCEs for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ROCE of 12-15% and FY28 target of 20%, with ROCE returning to historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 278 crore auto order be domestic or export?
qa_highlights.answer: Entirely domestic: ~82% passenger vehicle and ~18% two-wheeler; the two-wheeler business is crankshafts from the Gurugram machining facility. Management says the PV order is EV, which is domestic-brand supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV vs ICE mix in passenger vehicles and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: PV order book is about 50:50 ICE and EV. Export sales have so far been more EV-led, with bulk ICE supply starting.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt fall to Rs 1,000 crore in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No target given; management said it is not aiming for a zero-debt company but will keep leverage under check while growing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Rs 8,000 crore turnover target?
qa_highlights.answer: Target moved to FY29 (one year later), implying 22-25% CAGR from last year's turnover of about Rs 4,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 margin improving given market conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: No improvement in market conditions yet. Management said energy and shipping costs will not moderate unless geopolitical issues are resolved.

risks_watch: Energy and shipping costs not yet passed on; management said they will not moderate unless the geopolitical situation (West Asia) is resolved, so EBITDA margin gains depend on cost relief.
Steel passes through with a one-quarter lag and cannot be hedged; a sharp steel move could swing quarterly margins in either direction.
Working capital pressure from shipping delays and longer transit times; management gave internal targets of 15-20 days improvement but no firm timeline.
Execution on new ventures: aluminium forging bulk supply started, aerospace/semiconductor/robotics revenue 12-18 months away, Inconel/titanium 8-10 quarters away; zero aerospace order book currently.
Mexico revenue ramp (about Rs 6 crore this quarter, significant revenue from Q3 FY27) and rail wheel JV bulk production targeted Sept/Oct 2026 are timeline commitments to track.
Casting realisations fell QoQ due to one-off components during ramp-up; management expects recovery next quarter. Ring rolling at 127% utilisation with no capacity addition planned.
key_quotes: So, we would not like to guide the market in terms of profitability.
No, I think we have not seen any improvement in terms of market conditions.
No, I think this margin is sustainable margin and you will see improvement on it going forward.
I think it is at least 12 months to 18 months before we have a significant revenue or product lines from this section.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and export outlook, but cautious and evasive on margins: management refused to give a full-year margin range or profitability guidance and said Q2 market conditions had not improved. Deliberately vague on timelines for working capital targets and the non-ferrous ramp.

growth.why: Management guides to ~20% plus export growth, Rs 8,000 crore FY29 turnover target (22-25% CAGR), and cold forging utilisation above 70% by Q3 FY27, but ring rolling is at 127% with no new capacity planned, and the wheel JV and aluminium ramps are later-dated, so growth is positive but mostly unquantified beyond exports.
